body.en: Power series represent transcendental and non-polynomial functions as infinite polynomials. On the AP Calculus BC exam, mastering power series, Taylor and Maclaurin polynomials, term-by-term calculus, and bounding truncation errors via the Lagrange Error Bound is essential for Question 6 on the Free-Response section.
body.ar: Power المتسلسلة represent transcendental and non-كثيرة الحدود الدوال as infinite polynomials. On the AP التفاضل والتكامل BC exam, mastering power المتسلسلة, Taylor and Maclaurin polynomials, term-by-term التفاضل والتكامل, and bounding truncation errors via the Lagrange Error Bound is essential for Question 6 on the Free-Response section.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Power Series, Radius & Interval of Convergence

body.en: A power series centered at \(x = c\) is an infinite series of the form \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n (x - c)^n\). Its domain of convergence is always an interval centered at \(c\).
body.ar: A power المتسلسلة centered at \(x = c\) is an infinite المتسلسلة of the form \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n (x - c)^n\). Its المجال of convergence is always an interval centered at \(c\).

label.en: ● Theorem · Convergence of Power Series & Endpoint Protocol
label.ar: ● مبرهنة · Convergence of Power المتسلسلة & Endpoint Protocol

body.en:
Theorem: For any power series \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n (x - c)^n\), exactly one of three cases holds:
1. The series converges only at the center \(x = c\) (\(R = 0\)).
2. The series converges absolutely for all real numbers \(x\) (\(R = \infty\)).
3. There exists a real number \(R > 0\) (the radius of convergence) such that the series converges absolutely for \(|x - c| < R\) and diverges for \(|x - c| > R\).

The Mandatory 3-Step Protocol for Finding the Interval of Convergence:
• Step 1 (Find Radius \(R\)): Apply the Ratio Test: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}(x - c)^{n+1}}{a_n(x - c)^n} \right| = |x - c| \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right|. \] Set \(L < 1\) to solve for \(|x - c| < R\).
• Step 2 (Establish Open Interval): \(c - R < x < c + R\).
• Step 3 (Test Endpoints Individually): Substitute \(x = c - R\) and \(x = c + R\) separately into the original series. The Ratio Test is always inconclusive (\(L = 1\)) at endpoints, so use the \(p\)-series test, Alternating Series Test, or comparison tests to decide whether to include brackets \([\dots]\) or parentheses \((\dots)\).
body.ar:
Theorem: For any power المتسلسلة \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n (x - c)^n\), exactly one of three cases holds:
1. The المتسلسلة converges only at the center \(x = c\) (\(R = 0\)).
2. The المتسلسلة converges absolutely for all real numbers \(x\) (\(R = \infty\)).
3. There exists a real number \(R > 0\) (the radius of convergence) such that the المتسلسلة converges absolutely for \(|x - c| < R\) and diverges for \(|x - c| > R\).

The Mandatory 3-Step Protocol for Finding the Interval of Convergence:
• Step 1 (Find نصف القطر \(R\)): Apply the Ratio Test: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}(x - c)^{n+1}}{a_n(x - c)^n} \right| = |x - c| \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} \right|. \] Set \(L < 1\) to أوجد قيمة \(|x - c| < R\).
• Step 2 (Establish Open Interval): \(c - R < x < c + R\).
• Step 3 (Test Endpoints Individually): عوّض \(x = c - R\) and \(x = c + R\) separately into the original المتسلسلة. The Ratio Test is always inconclusive (\(L = 1\)) at endpoints, so use the \(p\)-المتسلسلة test, Alternating المتسلسلة Test, or comparison tests to decide whether to include brackets \([\dots]\) or parentheses \((\dots)\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Unit 10 · Power Series, Taylor & Maclaurin Series)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Unit 10 · Power المتسلسلة, Taylor & Maclaurin المتسلسلة)

body.en:
Why the Geometric Sum Formula & \(S_\infty\) Work: Write \(S_n = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^{n-1}\). Multiplying through by \(r\) shifts every power up by one:

\[ S_n - rS_n = (a + ar + \dots + ar^{n-1}) - (ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^n) = a - ar^n \]

Factoring \(S_n(1 - r) = a(1 - r^n)\) gives \(S_n = \dfrac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}\) for \(r \ne 1\). Taking \(n \to \infty\), \(\lim_{n \to \infty} r^n = 0\) holds if and only if \(|r| < 1\), yielding \(S_\infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}\).
body.ar:
Why the Geometric Sum الصيغة & \(S_\infty\) Work: Write \(S_n = a + ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^{n-1}\). Multiplying through by \(r\) shifts every power up by one:

\[ S_n - rS_n = (a + ar + \dots + ar^{n-1}) - (ar + ar^2 + \dots + ar^n) = a - ar^n \]

Factoring \(S_n(1 - r) = a(1 - r^n)\) gives \(S_n = \dfrac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}\) for \(r \ne 1\). Taking \(n \to \infty\), \(\lim_{n \to \infty} r^n = 0\) holds if and only if \(|r| < 1\), yielding \(S_\infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}\).

label.en: Level 1 (Foundations) — Worked Example · Radius & Interval with Endpoint Analysis
label.ar: Level 1 (Foundations) — مثال محلول · نصف القطر & Interval with Endpoint Analysis

body.en:
Problem: Find the radius of convergence and interval of convergence of \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n}\).

Step 1 · Ratio Test: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{(x - 2)^{n+1}}{(n+1)3^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 3^n}{(x - 2)^n} \right| = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( \frac{n}{n+1} \cdot \frac{|x - 2|}{3} \right) = \frac{|x - 2|}{3}. \] Set \(L < 1\): \[ \frac{|x - 2|}{3} < 1 \implies |x - 2| < 3 \implies \mathbf{R = 3}. \] The open interior interval is \(-3 < x - 2 < 3 \implies -1 < x < 5\).

Step 2 · Test Left Endpoint \(x = -1\): \[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1 - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-3)^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{n}. \] This is the alternating harmonic series, which converges by the AST. Thus, \(x = -1\) is included: \([-1\).

Step 3 · Test Right Endpoint \(x = 5\): \[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(5 - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{3^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n}. \] This is the harmonic series (\(p\)-series with \(p = 1\)), which diverges. Thus, \(x = 5\) is excluded: \(5)\).

Conclusion: \(\mathbf{R = 3}\), and the interval of convergence is \(\mathbf{[-1, 5)}\).
body.ar:
Problem: أوجد نصف القطر of convergence and interval of convergence of \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n}\).

Step 1 · Ratio Test: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{(x - 2)^{n+1}}{(n+1)3^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n \cdot 3^n}{(x - 2)^n} \right| = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( \frac{n}{n+1} \cdot \frac{|x - 2|}{3} \right) = \frac{|x - 2|}{3}. \] Set \(L < 1\): \[ \frac{|x - 2|}{3} < 1 \implies |x - 2| < 3 \implies \mathbf{R = 3}. \] The open interior interval is \(-3 < x - 2 < 3 \implies -1 < x < 5\).

Step 2 · Test Left Endpoint \(x = -1\): \[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1 - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-3)^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n}{n}. \] This is the alternating harmonic المتسلسلة, which converges by the AST. وعليه, \(x = -1\) is included: \([-1\).

Step 3 · Test Right Endpoint \(x = 5\): \[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(5 - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{3^n}{n \cdot 3^n} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n}. \] This is the harmonic المتسلسلة (\(p\)-المتسلسلة with \(p = 1\)), which diverges. وعليه, \(x = 5\) is excluded: \(5)\).

Conclusion: \(\mathbf{R = 3}\), and the interval of convergence is \(\mathbf{[-1, 5)}\).

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — Unit 10 · Power Series, Taylor & Maclaurin Series (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(B\) — Unit 10 · Power المتسلسلة, Taylor & Maclaurin المتسلسلة (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Consider the function \( f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} \). Which of the following is the Maclaurin series for \( \cos(x) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: The Maclaurin series for \( f(x) \) is a Taylor series expansion around \( x=0 \). We are given the series \( f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} \). Expanding this series, we get: For \( n=0 \): \( \frac{(-1)^0 x^{2(0)}}{(2(0))!} = \frac{x^0}{0!} = \frac{1}{1} = 1 \) For \( n=1 \): \( \frac{(-1)^1 x^{2(1)}}{(2(1))!} = \frac{-x^2}{2!} = -\frac{x^2}{2} \) For \( n=2 \): \( \frac{(-1)^2 x^{2(2)}}{(2(2))!} = \frac{x^4}{4!} = \frac{x^4}{24} \) So, \( f(x) = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} - \cdot s \). This is the well-known Maclaurin series for \( \cos(x) \). Therefore, the given series is the Maclaurin series for \( \cos(x) \).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): Consider the الدالة \( f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} \). Which of the following is the Maclaurin المتسلسلة for \( \cos(x) \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: The Maclaurin المتسلسلة for \( f(x) \) is a Taylor المتسلسلة expansion around \( x=0 \). We are المعطيات the المتسلسلة \( f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} \). Expanding this المتسلسلة, we get: For \( n=0 \): \( \frac{(-1)^0 x^{2(0)}}{(2(0))!} = \frac{x^0}{0!} = \frac{1}{1} = 1 \) For \( n=1 \): \( \frac{(-1)^1 x^{2(1)}}{(2(1))!} = \frac{-x^2}{2!} = -\frac{x^2}{2} \) For \( n=2 \): \( \frac{(-1)^2 x^{2(2)}}{(2(2))!} = \frac{x^4}{4!} = \frac{x^4}{24} \) So, \( f(x) = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} - \cdot s \). This is the well-known Maclaurin المتسلسلة for \( \cos(x) \). وبالتالي, the المعطيات المتسلسلة is the Maclaurin المتسلسلة for \( \cos(x) \).

body.en:
1. Expanding \((a + bx)^n\) Without Factoring Out \(a^n\): For negative or fractional \(n\) on College Board AP Calculus BC, the formula \(1 + nu + \tfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}u^2 + \dots\) requires the first term inside the bracket to be 1: \((a + bx)^n = a^n\bigl(1 + \tfrac{b}{a}x\bigr)^n\). Omitting \(a^n\) loses almost all marks.

2. Confusing the \(n\)-th Term \(u_n\) with the Partial Sum \(S_n\): When given a formula for \(S_n\), extract \(u_n = S_n - S_{n-1}\) for \(n \ge 2\) and \(u_1 = S_1\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Find the radius of convergence \(R\) for the power series \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty n! (2x - 1)^n\).
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

أوجد radius of convergence \(R\) for the power series \(\sum_{n=0}^\infty n! (2x - 1)^n\).

solution.en: Apply the Ratio Test: \[ L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{(n+1)! (2x - 1)^{n+1}}{n! (2x - 1)^n} \right| = |2x - 1| \lim_{n\to\infty} (n+1). \] For any \(x eq \frac{1}{2}\), this limit is \(\infty\). The series converges only at its center \(x = \frac{1}{2}\). Thus, the radius of convergence is \(\mathbf{R = 0}\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Taylor & Maclaurin Polynomials & Standard Catalog Manipulations

body.en: A Taylor series approximates any sufficiently differentiable function \(f(x)\) locally by matching all higher-order derivatives at a chosen center \(x = c\). When \(c = 0\), it is termed a Maclaurin series.
body.ar: A Taylor المتسلسلة approximates any sufficiently differentiable الدالة \(f(x)\) locally by matching all higher-order المشتقات at a chosen center \(x = c\). عندما \(c = 0\), it is termed a Maclaurin المتسلسلة.

body.en:
Problem: Find the first four nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for \(f(x) = \int_0^x e^{-t^2}\,dt\).

Step 1 · Substitute \(-t^2\) into the \(e^u\) Series: Recall \(e^u = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{u^n}{n!} = 1 + u + \frac{u^2}{2!} + \frac{u^3}{3!} + \dots\). Let \(u = -t^2\): \[ e^{-t^2} = 1 + (-t^2) + \frac{(-t^2)^2}{2!} + \frac{(-t^2)^3}{3!} + \dots = 1 - t^2 + \frac{t^4}{2} - \frac{t^6}{6} + \dots = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n t^{2n}}{n!}. \]

Step 2 · Integrate Term-by-Term: \[ f(x) = \int_0^x \left( 1 - t^2 + \frac{t^4}{2} - \frac{t^6}{6} + \dots \right) dt = \left[ t - \frac{t^3}{3} + \frac{t^5}{10} - \frac{t^7}{42} + \dots \right]_0^x. \] \[ = \mathbf{x - \frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{x^5}{10} - \frac{x^7}{42} + \dots} = \mathbf{\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n+1}}{n!(2n + 1)}}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Find the third-degree Taylor polynomial \(P_3(x)\) for \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\) centered at \(c = 4\).
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

أوجد third-degree Taylor polynomial \(P_3(x)\) for \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\) centered at \(c = 4\).

hints.ar: احسب قيمة derivatives at \(c = 4\): • \(f(x) = x^{1/2} \implies f(4)\).
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} \implies f'(4) = \frac{1}{2(2)} = \frac{1}{4}\) ، \(f''(x) = -\frac{1}{4}x^{-3/2} \implies f''(4) = -\frac{1}{4(8)}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(= \mathbf{2 + \frac{1}{4}(x - 4) - \frac{1}{64}(x - 4)^2 + \frac{1}{512}(x - 4)^3}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(= \mathbf{2 + \frac{1}{4}(x - 4) - \frac{1}{64}(x - 4)^2 + \frac{1}{512}(x - 4)^3}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ — Lagrange Error Bound & Truncation Remainder Theorems

body.en: On AP Calculus BC Free Response Question 6, students must bound the difference between a function \(f(x)\) and its Taylor polynomial \(P_n(x)\) using either the Alternating Series Error Bound or the Lagrange Error Bound.
body.ar: On AP التفاضل والتكامل BC Free Response Question 6, students must bound the difference between a الدالة \(f(x)\) and its Taylor كثيرة الحدود \(P_n(x)\) using either the Alternating المتسلسلة Error Bound or the Lagrange Error Bound.

body.en:
Theorem: Let \(f(x)\) have \(n + 1\) continuous derivatives on an interval containing \(c\) and \(x\). Then: \[ f(x) = P_n(x) + R_n(x), \] where the remainder \(R_n(x)\) satisfies: \[ |R_n(x)| = |f(x) - P_n(x)| \le \frac{M}{(n+1)!} |x - c|^{n+1}, \] where \(M = \max |f^{(n+1)}(t)|\) for all \(t\) in the closed interval between \(c\) and \(x\).

AP Strategy: On FRQs, \(M\) is either provided explicitly as a maximum bound on \(f^{(n+1)}\) in a table/graph, or determined by taking the absolute maximum of a known derivative (e.g. \(|\sin(t)| \le 1\)).
body.ar:
Theorem: Let \(f(x)\) have \(n + 1\) continuous المشتقات on an interval containing \(c\) and \(x\). Then: \[ f(x) = P_n(x) + R_n(x), \] حيث the remainder \(R_n(x)\) satisfies: \[ |R_n(x)| = |f(x) - P_n(x)| \le \frac{M}{(n+1)!} |x - c|^{n+1}, \] حيث \(M = \max |f^{(n+1)}(t)|\) for all \(t\) in the closed interval between \(c\) and \(x\).

AP Strategy: On FRQs, \(M\) is either provided explicitly as a maximum bound on \(f^{(n+1)}\) in a الجدول/التمثيل البياني, or determined by taking the absolute maximum of a known المشتقة (e.g. \(|\sin(t)| \le 1\)).

body.en:
FRQ Prompt: Let \(f\) be a function with \(f(0) = 3\), \(f'(0) = -2\), \(f''(0) = 6\), and \(f'''(0) = -12\). The graph of \(f^{(4)}(x)\) on \([0, 0.5]\) is strictly decreasing with \(f^{(4)}(0) = 48\) and \(f^{(4)}(0.5) = 16\).
(a) Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial \(P_3(x)\) for \(f\) about \(x = 0\).
(b) Use \(P_3(0.5)\) to approximate \(f(0.5)\).
(c) Use the Lagrange Error Bound to show that \(|f(0.5) - P_3(0.5)| \le \frac{1}{8}\).

Part (a) · Third-Degree Taylor Polynomial: \[ P_3(x) = 3 + (-2)x + \frac{6}{2!}x^2 + \frac{-12}{3!}x^3 = \mathbf{3 - 2x + 3x^2 - 2x^3}. \]

Part (b) · Approximation at \(x = 0.5\): \[ P_3(0.5) = 3 - 2(0.5) + 3(0.5)^2 - 2(0.5)^3 = 3 - 1 + 3(0.25) - 2(0.125) = 2 + 0.75 - 0.25 = \mathbf{2.5}. \]

Part (c) · Lagrange Error Bound Justification: Since \(f^{(4)}(x)\) is positive and strictly decreasing on \([0, 0.5]\), its maximum absolute value occurs at \(x = 0\): \[ M = \max_{t \in [0, 0.5]} |f^{(4)}(t)| = f^{(4)}(0) = 48. \] Apply the Lagrange formula with \(n = 3, c = 0, x = 0.5\): \[ |R_3(0.5)| \le \frac{M}{(3+1)!}|0.5 - 0|^4 = \frac{48}{4!} (0.5)^4 = \frac{48}{24} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 = 2 \left(\frac{1}{16}\right) = \frac{2}{16} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{8}}. \] Since \(|f(0.5) - P_3(0.5)| \le \frac{1}{8}\), the proof is complete.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

Let \(P_4(x)\) be the fourth-degree Maclaurin polynomial for \(\cos(x)\). Use the Lagrange Error Bound to prove that \(|\cos(0.5) - P_4(0.5)| < \frac{1}{3000}\).
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced / AP FRQ

ليكن \(P_4(x)\) be the fourth-degree Maclaurin polynomial for \(\cos(x)\). Use the Lagrange Error Bound to prove that \(|\cos(0.5) - P_4(0.5)| < \frac{1}{3000}\).

solution.en: For \(f(x) = \cos(x)\), \(f^{(5)}(x) = -\sin(x)\). Since \(|-\sin(t)| \le 1\) for all \(t\), we take \(M = 1\). Apply the Lagrange Error Bound formula with \(n = 4, c = 0, x = 0.5\): \[ |R_4(0.5)| \le \frac{M}{(4+1)!}|0.5 - 0|^{4+1} = \frac{1}{5!} (0.5)^5 = \frac{1}{120} \left(\frac{1}{32}\right) = \frac{1}{3840}. \] Because \(3840 > 3000\), it follows that: \[ \frac{1}{3840} < \frac{1}{3000} \implies \mathbf{|\cos(0.5) - P_4(0.5)| < \frac{1}{3000}}. \]
solution.ar:

question.en: [Practice 4 · Easy] The Maclaurin series for a function \( f(x) \) is given by \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(0)}{n!} x^n \). If the first three terms of the Maclaurin series for \( f(x) \) are \( 5 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 \), what are the values of \( f(0) \), \( f'(0) \), and \( f''(0) \)?
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Easy] The Maclaurin series for a function \( f(x) \) is given by \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(0)}{n!} x^n \). إذا كان the first three حدود من Maclaurin series for \( f(x) \) are \( 5 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 \), what are the values of \( f(0) \), \( f'(0) \), and \( f''(0) \)?

hints.en: The Maclaurin series for a function \( f(x) \) is given by \( f(x) = f(0) + \frac{f'(0)}{1!}x + \frac{f''(0)}{2!}x^2 + \frac{f'''(0)}{3!}x^3 + \dots \). We are given the first three terms of the Maclaurin series as \( 5 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 \). Comparing the coefficients term by term: For the constant term (x^0): \( f(0) = 5 \).
hints.ar: The Maclaurin series for a function \( f(x) \) is given by \( f(x) = f(0) + \frac{f'(0)}{1!}x + \frac{f''(0)}{2!}x^2 + \frac{f'''(0)}{3!}x^3 + \dots \). We are given the first three حدود من Maclaurin series as \( 5 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 \). Comparing the coefficients term by term: For the constant term (x^0): \( f(0) = 5 \).

hints.en: For the x term (x^1): \( \frac{f'(0)}{1!} = -2 \Rightarrow f'(0) = -2 \). For the x^2 term (x^2): \(\frac{f''(0)}{2!} = \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{f''(0)}{2} = \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow f''(0)\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( \frac{f'(0)}{1!} = -2 \Rightarrow f'(0) = -2 \) ، \(\frac{f''(0)}{2!} = \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{f''(0)}{2} = \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow f''(0)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
The Maclaurin series for a function \( f(x) \) is given by \( f(x) = f(0) + \frac{f'(0)}{1!}x + \frac{f''(0)}{2!}x^2 + \frac{f'''(0)}{3!}x^3 + \dots \). We are given the first three terms of the Maclaurin series as \( 5 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 \). Comparing the coefficients term by term:

For the constant term (x^0): \( f(0) = 5 \).

For the x term (x^1): \( \frac{f'(0)}{1!} = -2 \Rightarrow f'(0) = -2 \).

For the x^2 term (x^2): \( \frac{f''(0)}{2!} = \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{f''(0)}{2} = \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow f''(0) = 3 \).

Therefore, \( f(0) = 5, f'(0) = -2, f''(0) = 3 \).
